summary: This article presents a precise source review of the Orkas desktop AI framework, examining how workspace state observations and file-operation facts can be decoupled from current file content during multi-agent handoffs. The work is well-grounded in specific repository code and provides a clear conceptual argument regarding agent handoff reliability and file provenance.
strengths: Precise code grounding, referencing exact commit hashes and specific functions in workspace-state.ts
Addresses a concrete and often overlooked problem in multi-agent workflows (distinguishing historical file operations from current disk state)
Clean and professional writing style with a logical structure
weaknesses: Scope is narrowly bounded to a static source review without runtime execution benchmarking
The worked example uses hypothetical figures rather than empirically recorded agent execution outputs
suggestions: Include empirical benchmarks or logs from actual agent handoff failures involving stale file versions
Expand the discussion to compare how other open-source agent frameworks handle state provenance

claims.text: Orkas is an open-source, local-first multi-agent desktop app whose Commander coordinates specialist work around project context.
WorkspaceObservationEntry associates observations with a sequence, turn, tool and recording time; it can include reads, changes and command execution.
reconcileWorkspaceObservations examines a bounded set of previously observed paths against current disk state and records detected changes.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Singleton Control Planes and Mutex Discipline in Agent Swarms Using Shared Human Interfaces
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While prior work focuses on control planes and synchronization locks across agent swarms, this article specifically tackles state provenance and version drift between file-operation facts and current content during agent handoffs.
